mismatch.message: simple monster action requires uhitm.c mhitm_ad_acid()

summary: The admitted v83 stop is the unported uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_acid function. At segment 0 step 1304 the tame ochre jelly lands its AD_ACID engulf attack on a hostile gray ooze; C continues into the acid-resistant monster-versus-monster branch, prints that the acid seems harmless, zeroes direct damage, and still performs its armor-corrosion and weapon-acid checks. JavaScript stopped at the AD_ACID arm in mhitm_adtyping before those source effects.

source.branch: The relevant branch has a non-hero attacker and a non-hero defender. C returns early with zero damage when the aggressor is cancelled. Otherwise, acid resistance or AD_ACID defense suppresses direct damage and, when visible, emits the harmless-acid message; a vulnerable visible defender gets the covered-in-acid and burning messages. Regardless of resistance, the branch then rolls rn2(30) for armor corrosion and rn2(6) for acid damage to the defender's weapon. The same function also handles hero-attacker and hero-defender cases, so its full implementation must preserve those branches and source order.
callers: mhitm.c:mattackm -> hitmm -> mdamagem -> uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping selects mhitm_ad_acid for the admitted monster-versus-monster attack.
mhitu.c:mattacku -> hitmu -> uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping is a source caller for monster attacks on the hero; the natural ochre-jelly AT_ENGL AD_ACID attack instead routes through mhitu.c:gulpmu.
uhitm.c:damageum -> uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping is a source caller for polymorphed hero attacks; the current monster table has no ordinary AD_ACID melee form that reaches this route.
dependencies: mondata.c:Resists_Elem implements resists_acid; mondata.c:defended checks artifact defense.
uhitm.c:erode_armor applies the rn2(30) armor-corrosion outcome.
trap.c:acid_damage handles acid damage to the target's weapon after the rn2(6) check.
pline.c:pline and pline_mon produce the visible acid messages; mhitu.c:hitmsg covers the monster-attacks-hero branch.

evidence: The current official v83 evaluation identifies synthetic/v83/v83-mm-acid-resistant-action1, segment 0, first mismatch step 1304. The accepted recording SHA-256 is edc33a32ccbf0823b497427a6c23e8091ee5039399fcbe638c8583b0e38cd3c0; manifest SHA-256 is b7cbc7c9d30cbf9a85a343d23133465671ed29eebe3a83200de2fa7575c76329. Baseline results are 1304/1693 screens, 3151/3326 RNG calls, and 1304/1693 cursors before the non-null stop.

The unchanged C recording at step 1304 shows 'The ochre jelly engulfs the gray ooze.' The following C message at step 1305 is 'The gray ooze is covered in acid, but it seems harmless.' That sequence identifies the actor, defender, engulf AD_ACID branch, and acid resistance outcome without relying on the case name.

At step 1305 the C recording logs rn2(30)=11 at uhitm.c:2781 and rn2(6)=0 at uhitm.c:2783. These occur after the resistance branch sets damage to zero, proving the corrosion and weapon-acid checks still run for an acid-resistant defender.

Source inspection confirms the missing implementation is uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_acid and the production gap is the AD_ACID refusal in js/uhitm.js:mhitm_adtyping. The other damage-type arms in that dispatcher are already routed to source-named implementations. The implementation must remove this refusal and wire the ported function through the same dispatcher.

The admitted v83 recording is the only cited runtime range for this helper: segment 0 steps 1304-1305 pass through the mhitm.c:mattackm -> hitmm -> mdamagem caller and exercise the resistant monster-versus-monster branch. The source-correct output and both acid checks match.

Hero-attacker and hero-defender branches are implemented from C but lack matching production ranges. The previously attempted v33 ochre-jelly attack reaches uhitm.c:gulpum, not mhitm_ad_acid. The two blocked hero-defender recipes document why the ordinary AT_ENGL route uses mhitu.c:gulpmu and why the unstuck mspec_used cooldown is decremented by mcalcdistress -> mon_regen before the next attack. No range from those attempts is claimed.
The implementation and source-pinned test are in commit 2e5fb2e3d298341b1729057b57f6d5a682a0448c. Focused test `node --test scripts/uhitm-ad-acid.test.mjs` passed five tests; `npm run lint` passed.

Required range verification `node scripts/synthetic-range-evidence.mjs .cache/task-evidence.json` matched v83/v83-mm-acid-resistant-action1 segment 0 through step 1305 on the current implementation. The full selected recipe replay also matched all recorded screens, RNG calls and cursors (run-JHXceh).

The source-pinned tests directly check the helper branches but are not production runtime evidence. The blocked hero-defender recipes are recipes/uhitm.c/mhitm-ad-acid-hero-defender-blocked-wizard.session.json and recipes/uhitm.c/mhitm-ad-acid-hero-defender-blocked-monk-variation.session.json; no recording from either attempt is cited.
